shifts.summary: The paper was overall judged moderate, with candidates reporting good attempts between 65 and 82. Reasoning was mostly easy but some found it moderate to difficult, and attempts ranged 17–24. Quantitative aptitude was widely seen as difficult, with time pressure limiting attempts to about 15–20. English was consistently described as easy, focusing on synonym‑antonym and passage items.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was described as easy and doable within 10‑11 minutes by some candidates, while others found it moderate to difficult and lengthy.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: General Awareness featured factual GK, current affairs from 2025, and policy questions such as Swachh Bharat, with some candidates finding it easy and others difficult.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math section had long questions, time pressure of 15 min, candidates could attempt about 15‑16 questions, with many reporting difficulty.

topics.topic: Regular hexagon divided into 6 equilateral triangles

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English comprised synonym‑antonym, one‑word substitution, idioms and a passage, and was generally considered easy.

observations: Overall paper was judged moderate with good attempts ranging 65–82.
Reasoning was generally easy but some candidates found it moderate to difficult, leading to 17–24 attempts.
Quantitative aptitude was widely seen as difficult, with time shortage limiting attempts to about 15–20.
English was consistently described as easy, focusing on synonym‑antonym and passage items.
disagreements: Reasoning: 3 reports called it easy, 2 called it moderate to difficult, 1 called it easy to moderate.
General Awareness: 3 reports called it easy, 2 called it difficult, 1 called it moderate to hard.
Quantitative: 4 reports called it difficult, 1 called it moderate to difficult, 1 called it hard.
English: 4 reports called it easy, 2 called it moderate to difficult, 1 called it moderate.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 23 October 2026 was reported as moderate overall across the shifts that have published data. Unofficial figures suggest good attempts ranged from about 65 to 82 for Shift 1 and 66 to 72 for Shift 2, but the SSC normalises scores across shifts, so direct comparison is limited. Reasoning was generally seen as easy to moderate, while Quantitative Aptitude was perceived as more difficult with notable time pressure. English was consistently described as easy, focusing on synonym‑antonym and passage items. No usable analysis is available yet for Shift 3, pending further candidate evidence.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both reported shifts (Shift 1 and Shift 2) described the paper as moderate overall. Shift 3 is still pending, so no analysis is available for that shift yet.

faqs.q: How did candidates find the Reasoning section on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning was largely reported as easy to moderate. In Shift 1 it was mostly easy, while Shift 2 had mixed reports ranging from easy to moderate.

faqs.q: What was the perceived difficulty of Quantitative Aptitude on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative Aptitude was widely regarded as difficult. Candidates in Shift 1 noted time pressure limiting attempts to about 15–20 questions, and Shift 2 reported difficulty ranging from moderate to difficult with 15–19 good attempts.

faqs.q: How did candidates rate the English section on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: English was consistently described as easy across the reported shifts, focusing on synonym‑antonym and passage items, with good attempts in the high teens to low twenties.
